posts.title: FORS hash forests
posts.summary: FORS is a few-time hash-based signature: a forest of Merkle trees, parameterized by k and a, stepped through in the browser.
posts.description: In contrast to one-time WOTS, FORS lets you sign a few times. Walk indexes, secrets, auth paths, and the public key in an interactive forest.

posts.title: Why WOTS is one-time
posts.summary: Sign two real messages with the same WOTS key and watch an observer forge others from the leaked chain nodes.
posts.description: Sign two real messages with the same WOTS key and watch how an observer forges others from the leaked chain nodes.

posts.title: WOTS hash chains
posts.summary: An interactive look at real SHRINCS WOTS-TW hash chains, with step-by-step signing traces in the browser.
posts.description: Sign a message with WOTS-TW and step through real hash chains: digits, checksum, signatures, and public tips.

posts.title: Source code to pdf
posts.summary: A small command-line recipe for turning source trees into highlighted PDF documents.
posts.description: A compact walkthrough for concatenating code, highlighting it with Pygments, and exporting a PDF.

posts.title: Secure Machine Learning
posts.summary: An overview of how secure multiparty computation and privacy techniques can be applied to machine learning systems.
posts.description: A post about secure training, secure models, and secure querying for privacy-preserving machine learning.

posts.title: Oblivious Transfer
posts.summary: A practical introduction to oblivious transfer through a privacy-preserving weather application.
posts.description: An introduction to oblivious transfer with examples, code snippets, and a motivating application.

posts.title: Absolute Security with No Trust
posts.summary: A discussion of information-theoretic security and the practical trade-offs behind absolute security claims.
posts.description: A post about the promise and limits of absolute security without trusting third parties.
